title: Hiring for Temperament, Not Availability — What Changes at the Door
content:
###  **The Default Hiring Question** 

When a company needs field staff, the first question asked is almost always some version of: who is available and willing to do this? 

That question produces a pool. It does not produce a good one. 

### **The Better Question** 

The question worth asking is different: who would actually enjoy this? Who is going to have a better day because they spent it talking to sixty people, rather than a worse one? 

That question eliminates most applicants immediately. It also produces a completely different quality of conversation at the door. 

###  **Why Homeowners Notice Immediately** 

A homeowner opening their door can tell within seconds whether the person in front of them wants to be there. Someone who is genuinely comfortable and interested reads as a neighbor. Someone counting down the hours reads as a solicitor — and gets treated accordingly. 

That distinction has nothing to do with what either person says. 

###  **The Trade-Off** 

Hiring this way means a slower process, more people passed over, and more effort spent on recruiting than most companies would consider reasonable. We consider it the core of the service rather than an overhead cost — because it is the part that determines whether any of the rest of it works.
